alice.cust: Hey support, in our org console several action buttons (New deployment, Billing, Invite) are grayed out for me on Project 'proj-456' even though I can call the API with my key and create resources via CLI.
ben.support: Sorry you're hitting that. Quick question — do you see a 403 if you try the action from the browser devtools network tab or when calling the console API directly?
alice.cust: From browser devtools the console POST to /api/projects/proj-456/actions returns HTTP 403. CLI using personal API key to /v1/projects/proj-456/deploy works fine.
ben.support: Can you paste the request/response snippet (headers omitted) or a curl you ran? Also, are you in the same org role that used to have project-admin rights before the org migration last week?
alice.cust: here's a minimal repro I did:
```
curl -i -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/projects/proj-456/actions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_personal_xxx" \
  -d '{"action":"new_deploy"}'

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"forbidden","message":"missing project scope: projects.proj-456.admin"}
```
ben.support: That error string helps. CLI uses the API key scope and succeeds; console UI uses the browser session (SSO) token — so this looks like a permissions mismatch between SSO group mappings and the project's current identifier.
ben.support: Did the org undergo an ID/slug change during the transfer? I recall we did a migration where some project IDs were re-prefixed.
alice.cust: Yes — we did an org split last week and engineering renamed several project slugs (old ids had the org shortname prefix). My SSO group mappings might still be targeting the old slug.
carmen.oncall: Jumping in — we've seen this pattern. SCIM/SSO group-to-role mapping is keyed by exact project identifier. If your IdP is still sending groups like "redwood-old-proj-123-admins" but the project is now "proj-456" the mapping won't grant the project-level role and the console will block UI actions (403) even though org-level perms look ok.
ben.support: Can you check the group names we have recorded for you? @alice.cust run:
```
GET /internal/admin/users/alice.cust/sso-groups
```
and paste the output.
alice.cust: Output shows: ["redwood-old-proj-123-admins", "eng-team"]
ben.support: Yep that's the issue — the group name still references old project id. Two options:
- Short-term workaround: someone with org-admin invite you directly to the project (Project Settings -> Members -> Invite) which uses email assignation and will attach the correct project role.
- Fix: Update your IdP group naming or the SCIM mapping rules so the group sent by IdP matches the project's new slug, then re-sync.
carmen.oncall: I'll open an internal ticket to add a small diagnostic to the console that surfaces "SSO group matched: none for project proj-456" to make this easier next time. For now, if you can't change IdP mapping quickly, ask an org-admin to do the direct invite — that should restore UI actions immediately.
alice.cust: Thanks — org-admin invited me and buttons are enabled again. Can you keep the ticket open until there's a longer-term fix? :thumbsup:
ben.support: Will do. Filing ENG-4621 to track a better diagnostic + admin hint. Marking this thread resolved once ENG confirms.
idp-sync-bot: SCIM sync completed for org acme-corp at 2026-03-17T15:12:30Z "0 groups mapped to proj-456"
